title: AI Rule Review
summary: Reviews a batch of proposed Fusion AI rules against the existing set: maps each one, finds conflicts and gaps, recommends fixes, and gets Swami's decision.
what_it_is: A Claude skill for checking new rule proposals for the **Fusion AI Rules** before they join the set. A proposal can come from the Rule Set page's Propose on GitHub button, a file, pasted text, or someone's dashboard.

Claude files each proposal as a candidate, compares it with every active rule, writes up each conflict with fix options, and asks Swami once on a decision card. It then builds the accepted batch on a branch with the AI Rules Manager steps, ready for Swami to merge.
why: Proposals often overlap or contradict rules that already work. Izzy's Symmetry and Mirror batch clashed with two existing rules; this skill turns that kind of review into a repeatable process with one clear decision.

what_it_does.text: Copies each proposal verbatim into `candidates/<batch>/` with a C- ID, the author's own label, and the next free R number as its proposed ID.
Marks each candidate as New, Tightens, Overlaps or Conflicts against every active rule, and records `conflicts_with` and `related`.
Writes up each conflict with both texts quoted and 2 or 3 fix options, recommending the one that keeps Must rules intact and changes the least.
Checks priority, clarity, Fusion feature names as they appear in the UI, which AIs it works in, and length (about 600 characters or less).
Runs `python3 build/build.py check` with the candidates in place, so IDs and references are valid.
Asks Swami once on a decision card, recommending "accept with the recommended fixes", and keeps working on that option meanwhile.
Builds the accepted batch with the AI Rules Manager steps and opens a pull request, unmerged until Swami decides and the author agrees to CC BY 4.0.
Makes sure each accepted rule gets a test question in `tests/prompts/`, following the AI Rules Manager steps.
For a large batch, or to share with the author, builds a Rule Review dashboard with the vibe-dashboard skill.

triggers: "Izzy proposed some rules, check them against the set"
"Look at the new proposals on GitHub"

how_to_use.step: Point Claude at the proposals: GitHub issues, a file, pasted text, or a dashboard link.
Claude files the candidates, maps them, writes up conflicts and checks fit and the build.
Pick an option on the decision card. The recommended one is accept with the recommended fixes.
Confirm the author agrees to CC BY 4.0 for their rule text.
Claude builds the branch and opens a pull request; you merge it, or tell Claude to.

how_to_use_windows.step: Nothing runs on your computer, so the steps are the same on Windows 10 or 11.

capabilities.text: Boils a batch down to a single decision card with a recommended option, so Swami answers once.
Keeps the author's original text, labels and a decisions table in `sources/`, so every accepted rule can be traced back.
The build check runs with the candidates in place, and nothing merges without Swami.

limitations.text: Mapping and fix options are Claude's recommendations; Swami makes the decision.
It doesn't test a candidate in each AI; new rules start as Untested until test runs are recorded.
An outside author's rules can't merge until they agree to CC BY 4.0.

gotchas.text: Never change the author's meaning while filing candidates; fixes come later, as recommendations.
Check parameters and math (R08, R09), mirroring and timeline order, intersect or cut intent, and naming closely: that's where conflicts hide.
Deprecating or rewording an existing rule to fit a candidate is a major version bump.
Never put private links or names under NDA into anything that goes into the public repository.

requirements.text: Swami's GitHub connected to Claude, with the fusion-ai-rules repository attached with push access.
Nothing extra: works the same from Windows 10 or 11.

glossary.def: Swami's set of good-practice rules for AIs that model in Autodesk Fusion, kept in a public GitHub repository.
A proposed rule waiting for review, kept in `candidates/` with a C- ID and a proposed R number.
A group of proposals reviewed together, in one dated folder under `candidates/`.
A candidate that contradicts an existing rule; recorded in `conflicts_with` and resolved before release.
A candidate that makes an existing rule stricter or more specific.
A candidate that says the same thing as an existing rule.
The highest rule priority: something an AI gets wrong and that is costly. Shorter exports keep only Must rules.
A multiple-choice card in the Claude project where Swami picks an option, with one recommended.
A proposed set of changes on a branch, reviewed and checked before it is merged into main.
The Rule Set page's button that opens a prefilled proposal form on GitHub.
The open licence for the rule text: anyone can reuse it with credit. Authors of new rules agree to it.
An optional dashboard showing a batch's candidates, mapping, conflict cards and sign-off checklist.
The script step that validates every rule and candidate, and fails on errors such as taken IDs or broken references.

spoken._intro: This is the skill sheet for AI Rule Review, the skill that checks proposed rules before they join the Fusion AI Rules
spoken.What It Is: It turns a batch of proposals into one clear decision for you, then builds the accepted rules on a branch
spoken.What It Does: It files each proposal as a candidate, compares it with every active rule, writes up each conflict with fix options, checks fit and the build, and asks you once on a decision card
spoken.How to Use It: Point Claude at the proposals, pick an option on the decision card, confirm the author's consent to the open licence, and merge the pull request
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: Claude recommends and you decide. It doesn't test candidates in each AI, so new rules start as untested
